big_case.notes: Strickland v. Moritz raises institutionally sensitive questions about how the federal judiciary polices workplace sexual harassment and discrimination across its roughly 30,000 judicial-branch employees excluded from Title VII, naming senior Judicial Conference, Administrative Office, and Fourth Circuit officials as respondents and drawing congressional and GAO reform scrutiny. However, as presented at certiorari and resolved by a routine unexplained denial without dissent, the case carried minimal doctrinal reach: the Fifth Amendment challenge to Title VII's exclusion was held forfeited below (Pet. App. 44a-45a), the Congressional Accountability Act reporting theory (2 U.S.C. 1434) lacked a statutory right of action or lower-court ruling, no circuit split existed, only one amicus motion was filed at the certiorari stage, and the litigated due-process claim turned on fact-bound clear-error findings after petitioner withdrew from the Chapter X hearing process.
